**SECTION D: COMPOSITION (10 MARKS)**

Choose ONE of the following topics and write a composition of about 250-300 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: You attended a cultural festival in your village. You want to recount it to your friend, Peter, who could not be there. Write a letter to him describing the festival. You may want to give the name of the festival, when it took place, how the villagers prepared for it, what activities took place during this festival and finally, give your impressions about the festival. You are called Ngwa. Your address is GBHS Nyen, P.O. Box 900.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Une lettre personnelle (*personal letter*) suit une présentation imposée : l'adresse de l'expéditeur et la date en haut à droite, une formule d'appel amicale (« Dear Peter, »), un corps de lettre structuré en paragraphes, une formule de politesse finale et la signature. Le registre reste familier, chaleureux, à la différence d'une lettre formelle.

**Structure attendue :** adresse et date -> formule d'appel -> paragraphe d'introduction (raison d'écrire) -> paragraphe sur le nom et la date du festival -> paragraphe sur les préparatifs -> paragraphe sur les activités du jour -> paragraphe d'impressions personnelles -> formule de clôture amicale -> signature. Les quatre points suggérés par le sujet doivent tous apparaître, dans un ordre logique.

**Modèle de rédaction (anglais), environ 280 mots :**

GBHS Nyen
P.O. Box 900

Dear Peter,

I hope this letter finds you in good health. I am writing to tell you about a wonderful cultural festival I attended in my village last month, since I know you were unable to come.

The festival, called the Ngondo Festival, is held every year to honour our ancestors and the spirits of the water. This year it took place over an entire weekend, and the whole village had been getting ready for weeks beforehand. Women prepared traditional dishes and brewed local drinks, young men repaired the canoes that would be used for the water procession, and the elders rehearsed the ancient songs and prayers with the youths.

On the day itself, the celebration opened with a colourful procession from the chief's palace down to the river, with everyone dressed in traditional attire. There were traditional wrestling matches, drumming and dancing competitions, and a canoe race on the river that drew loud cheers from the crowd. In the evening, the elders performed a solemn ceremony by the riverbank, pouring libations and offering prayers for peace and prosperity in the coming year.

Honestly, Peter, I was deeply moved by the whole experience. Seeing our traditions kept alive with such enthusiasm made me proud of where I come from, and it reminded me how important it is for young people like us to preserve our culture.

I really wish you could have been there. Perhaps you can join me next year, it is an experience you should not miss.

Take care and write back soon.

Your friend,
Ngwa

### Piège à éviter
N'oublie pas d'inclure l'adresse donnée dans le sujet (« GBHS Nyen, P.O. Box 900 ») en tête de la lettre et de signer avec le nom imposé (« Ngwa ») : ces éléments de présentation sont notés séparément du contenu et une lettre sans adresse ni signature perd des points, même si le récit du festival est excellent.

### Conseil
Respecte le fil des quatre points suggérés par le sujet (nom et date, préparatifs, activités, impressions) comme un plan tout prêt : cela garantit que tu abordes tout ce qui est attendu sans rien oublier, et cela structure naturellement ta lettre en paragraphes clairs.

questions.enonce_markdown: "All humans are born equal". This is a theme for a speech you are to deliver to your school mates attending a seminar on the United Nations' Day to sensitise them on the necessity for gender equality. Write a speech pointing to three practices in your community which do not respect this statement, to sensitise your classmates.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un discours formel (*formal speech*) s'adresse à un public réuni pour une occasion précise. Il s'ouvre par une formule d'adresse au public, développe les points annoncés dans la consigne dans un ordre logique, et se termine par un remerciement ou un appel à l'action. Le registre reste soutenu, avec des formules d'adresse comme « ladies and gentlemen » ou « dear schoolmates ».

**Structure attendue :** formule d'adresse au public -> présentation du thème (« all humans are born equal ») -> les trois pratiques inégalitaires observées dans la communauté, une par paragraphe -> conséquences de ces pratiques -> appel à l'action ou au changement -> remerciement final. Le sujet impose exactement trois pratiques : elles doivent être clairement identifiées, pas seulement suggérées.

**Modèle de rédaction (anglais), environ 290 mots :**

Dear schoolmates, dear teachers,

Today, on this United Nations' Day, I would like to reflect with you on a simple but powerful statement: "All humans are born equal." If this is true, why do we still witness, in our own community, practices that treat men and women so differently? I want to point out three of these practices today.

First, in many families, girls are still withdrawn from school earlier than boys, either to help with housework or to be married off young, while their brothers are encouraged to pursue their studies as far as possible. This denies girls the same opportunities as boys, right from childhood.

Second, when it comes to inheritance, land and property are very often given only to sons, while daughters are excluded, as if they did not belong to the same family. This practice keeps women financially dependent on men throughout their lives.

Third, in many households, important decisions, whether about money, children's education or the family's future, are made by men alone, even when women contribute just as much to the family's wellbeing. Women's opinions are too often ignored simply because they are women.

These three practices contradict the very idea that all humans are born equal. Gender equality does not mean that men and women are identical, but that they deserve the same respect, the same opportunities and the same voice in decisions that concern them.

As the future leaders of our community, we have the power to change these habits: by supporting our sisters' education, by demanding fair inheritance for all children, and by including women in every decision that affects the family.

Thank you for your attention, and let us build a fairer community together.

### Piège à éviter
Ne te contente pas d'affirmer que l'inégalité existe sans donner d'exemples précis et concrets : le sujet demande explicitement trois pratiques identifiables, et un correcteur pénalise un discours qui reste dans les généralités sans les nommer clairement.

### Conseil
Ouvre et ferme ton discours en reprenant la citation du sujet (« all humans are born equal ») : cela montre au correcteur que tu réponds précisément à la consigne, et cela donne à ton discours une structure circulaire mémorable.

questions.enonce_markdown: Many people say that the only way to guarantee getting a good job is by completing a course of university education. Others claim that it is better to start work after secondary education and gain experience. How far do you agree or disagree with the above views. Give reasons for your choice and include any relevant examples from your knowledge and experience.
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un essai argumentatif se structure en trois parties : une introduction qui pose le débat et annonce la position défendue, un développement qui présente des arguments étayés par des exemples concrets, et une conclusion qui résume la position et l'ouvre éventuellement sur une nuance. Chaque paragraphe d'argument défend une seule idée, illustrée par au moins un exemple.

**Structure attendue :** introduction (présentation du débat université vs expérience directe, annonce de la position) -> développement en 2 ou 3 paragraphes d'arguments avec exemples -> conclusion (bilan et nuance éventuelle). Le sujet demande une prise de position claire (« how far do you agree or disagree »), pas seulement une liste d'arguments neutres.

**Modèle de rédaction (anglais), environ 300 mots :**

Getting a good job is a major concern for every young person, and opinions differ sharply on the best path to achieve it. While some believe that university education is the only guarantee of success, others argue that starting work early and gaining practical experience is a better option. In my opinion, both paths can lead to a good job, but practical experience often matters more than a university degree alone.

It is true that university education provides valuable theoretical knowledge and is required for certain professions, such as medicine or law, where years of specialised study are simply unavoidable. A doctor cannot practise safely without a solid academic foundation, and no amount of on-the-job experience can replace that.

However, in many other fields, practical experience is what employers value most. Many successful entrepreneurs and skilled technicians in Cameroon started working right after secondary school, learning their trade on the job, and today run thriving businesses without a university degree. Employers increasingly complain that some university graduates lack practical skills and take a long time to adapt to real working conditions, while someone who started early has already built years of hands-on competence and a professional network.

Moreover, completing a course of university education does not, by itself, guarantee a job: thousands of graduates in Cameroon remain unemployed every year, which shows that a degree alone is not a magic key to employment.

In conclusion, I largely disagree with the view that university education is the only guarantee of a good job. While it remains essential for certain specialised professions, practical experience gained early often proves just as valuable, if not more, in securing lasting professional success.

### Piège à éviter
Ne rédige pas un essai purement neutre qui se contente d'exposer les deux points de vue sans jamais trancher : le sujet demande explicitement « how far do you agree or disagree », ce qui impose une position personnelle clairement assumée, même nuancée.

### Conseil
Appuie chaque argument sur un exemple concret tiré de ton environnement (un métier, une personne, une situation observée au Cameroun) plutôt que de rester dans l'abstrait : c'est ce qui distingue un essai qui rapporte des points d'un essai qui reste vague et générique aux yeux du correcteur.
